intro.title: Multi-Tab Auth Sync
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Vue application that keeps a user's login status synchronized across multiple browser tabs. You will learn how to use the browser's localStorage API to share authentication state between tabs. The core concept involves listening for storage events to detect changes made in other tabs and updating your app's reactive state accordingly. You'll implement this by creating a Vue composable to manage the auth state and a component to display the login status. This will help you understand real-time state synchronization in a multi-tab environment using Vue's reactivity system.
intro.usecase: Multi-tab auth sync is essential for modern web applications where users frequently open multiple tabs. In banking dashboards, e-commerce sites, or collaborative tools like Google Workspace, logging out in one tab should immediately reflect across all open tabs to prevent security risks. This pattern ensures consistent authentication state in applications with real-time features like chat platforms or project management tools where session management is critical. Developers implement this to provide secure, seamless user experiences when switching between different views of the same application.
